messages.subject: Follow-up | Strategic Value Creation Brief for Safran
messages.body:
Dear Mr. Andriès,

Following my earlier introduction, I prepared a concise strategic value brief focused on Safran's production growth, defense expansion and international stakeholder priorities.

The paper addresses government and industrial-policy alignment, production capacity partnerships, local-value execution and sustainability evidence across international markets. These areas closely match my experience across government relations, ESG, corporate affairs, regulatory coordination and strategic partnerships.

My executive CV is included in the final three pages. I would welcome a confidential discussion regarding international leadership needs across government relations, external affairs, strategic partnerships, sustainability or country-facing execution.

Kind regards,
Ragunauth Ramsaroop
Liaison Director, Social Responsibility Department | AGM Inc.

strategic_brief.title: Strategic Value Creation Brief for Safran
strategic_brief.executive_summary: Safran is scaling across civil aerospace and defense while delivering strong financial performance and increasing production capacity. First-half 2026 results showed higher revenue, profitability and cash generation, supported by LEAP deliveries, defense electronics, military engines and aftermarket activity. Safran is also expanding international industrial partnerships and defense production capacity. This growth creates a broad external agenda spanning governments, regulators, suppliers, workforce ecosystems and local industrial partners. My director-level experience across government relations, ESG, corporate affairs and regulated stakeholder execution would support Safran by strengthening institutional alignment and converting external commitments into measurable delivery across priority markets.
strategic_brief.company_context: Safran reported first-half 2026 revenue of EUR 17.571 billion, up 19 percent, recurring operating income of EUR 3.237 billion and free cash flow of EUR 2.616 billion. LEAP deliveries reached 1,030 units in the first half, while defense activity grew across military engines, missile propulsion, navigation and optronics. Safran also continued international industrial expansion, including defense and helicopter-engine partnerships, while raising full-year guidance. Sustaining this pace requires coordination across industrial policy, government customers, production approvals, supplier capacity, workforce development and local partnerships. A consistent country-facing governance model can support growth while protecting delivery, reputation and the credibility of sustainability and local-value commitments.

opportunities.title: Government and industrial-policy alignment
opportunities.rationale: Safran's civil and defense businesses operate within national aerospace strategies, procurement systems, export frameworks and industrial policies. Production growth and defense demand increase the value of coordinated engagement with ministries, agencies, customers and local partners across priority markets.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would build country stakeholder architectures connecting government institutions, regulatory dependencies, customer priorities and internal business owners, with structured issue tracking and executive escalation so external engagement supports delivery and investment decisions.

opportunities.title: Production capacity stakeholder partnerships
opportunities.rationale: Higher engine, equipment and defense output requires suppliers, skilled labour, facilities and public-sector support. Capacity investments create opportunities to align workforce development, regional economic value and industrial partnerships with business requirements while strengthening confidence among customers and local institutions.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would coordinate government, workforce, supplier and community interfaces around capacity expansion, translating external expectations into measurable actions across operations, procurement, HR, sustainability and executive teams.

opportunities.title: International local value execution
opportunities.rationale: Aerospace and defense customers increasingly expect domestic capability, supplier participation and technology partnerships. Clear local-value governance helps Safran strengthen long-term market positions while ensuring commitments remain credible, measurable and connected to commercial and operational priorities.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would establish local-value plans with defined owners, evidence requirements and executive reporting across partnerships, procurement, workforce and stakeholder functions, informed by practical experience managing institutional and community commitments in a multinational operating environment.

opportunities.title: Sustainability evidence and assurance
opportunities.rationale: Aerospace growth and energy-transition pressure place increasing attention on environmental performance, operational efficiency and public commitments. Strong traceability between sustainability narratives and operating evidence supports regulators, customers, investors and communities while reducing reputation risk around complex claims.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would strengthen evidence ownership, data traceability and cross-functional accountability for material sustainability commitments, drawing on experience with environmental-management systems, carbon-data review and executive stakeholder communications.

days_0_30: Map priority markets, institutions, customers and industrial-policy dependencies.
Review material local-value, sustainability and capacity commitments.
Identify external risks with direct production, schedule or reputation impact.
days_31_60: Align government, business, sustainability and local-value engagement plans.
Create a consolidated commitment register with named owners and deadlines.
Define executive indicators for institutional alignment and external delivery.
days_61_90: Run focused engagement on priority industrial-policy and capacity issues.
Embed monthly cross-functional review of commitments and market risks.
Strengthen evidence controls for sustainability and local-value claims.
days_91_180: Scale the governance model across priority international markets.
Measure issue closure and commitment performance.
Codify lessons into a repeatable international stakeholder playbook.

potential_impact: Faster resolution of government and industrial-policy issues affecting growth.
Stronger local-value and workforce execution around production expansion.
Better alignment between external engagement and commercial delivery.
background_relevance: Director-level responsibility across government relations, ESG, corporate affairs and executive advisory in a multinational regulated business.
Direct engagement with ministries, regulators and public institutions around strategic projects and operating commitments.
Experience coordinating external expectations across procurement, operations, HR, environment, legal and executive teams.
Practical work on carbon-data traceability, environmental systems, local participation and stakeholder governance.
